items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Rex Stewart was on the left side of the other bandstand and that put him and I next to each other.

ctx.x: Sunday night I was at the Armory to hear Fletcher Henderson's orchestra for the second time. Naturally my place was right in front of the orchestra which was placed on the floor in the middle of the Armory. There was not a band stand because it was not a place where dances were given and the only one that I know of, that did take place there, was this dance that Fletcher was playing this night.

The sax section had not changed since the first time the band had played in Cincy. Another trombone had beed added and he was a young fellow named Benny Morton and Rex Stewart had replaced Joe Smith. My interest was mostly in the trumpet section and I noticed that Rex was extra fast in his execution and although I didn't know much about styles, I knew that his was different from Joe Smith and what I had heard Armstrong do on records. Rex was amusing to watch but I did not understand or care for the way he played.

But the band was just as great as it had been the first time I heard it and the Armory was crowded. We of the Helvey orchestra left Cincy for Lexington full of praise for Fletcher Henderson and his orchestra and we felt as though we had gotten religion and were on our way to heaven instead of Lexington.
